title: Common decline, divergent collapse: breeding-colony organization indexes local vulnerability across Antarctic penguin islands
revision_goals: make the island-ecology contribution explicit through seabird land-sea subsidy literature
quantify the small magnitude of the colony-network predictive increment rather than allowing the title or abstract to overstate it
keep failed environmental formulations distinct from claims that sea ice or terrestrial habitat are ecologically unimportant
treat Torgersen mapping as phenomenon-level spatial triangulation only
retain all frozen numerical endpoints and terminal development rule

new_context_references.role: general seabird-island ecology and marine-terrestrial coupling
systematic review of seabird effects on terrestrial breeding grounds

claims_allowed: five-island long-term decline has an exceptionally strong common component
annual dynamics and extinction endpoints differ among islands
tested simple sea-ice-duration and snowfall formulations are not supported in their predeclared directions
effective colony number adds a small positive held-out-year predictive increment of about 1.4 percent relative MSE reduction
independent Torgersen mapping shows real habitat-structured subcolony attrition
external spatial evidence is phenomenon-level triangulation
externally subsidized breeding islands provide a demographic complement to classic seabird-island ecosystem-engineering perspectives
claims_prohibited: sea ice is unimportant to Adelie ecology
effective colony number causally protects populations
the colony-network metric is externally validated at the colony-ID level
mapped habitat fragmentation is proven to cause the effective-colony signal
the supported colony-network signal explains the dominant regional decline
required_boundary: A public one-to-one crosswalk between Palmer LTER colony_code and independent GIS polygons remains unresolved.
terminal_rule: No new core endpoint family may be introduced during manuscript revision.
